fields.key_provisions: Introduced HB1515 would prohibit local final approval of a rezoning, special exception, special use permit, site plan, or plan of development for siting a new data center until the earlier of fulfillment of all pending data-center-customer requests for interconnection to electric utility distribution service or 2028-07-01. Data center is defined by reference to § 58.1-3506(A)(43).

fields.key_provisions: Introduced HB155 would require an SCC certificate before operating a facility, or facilities effectively operating together at the Commission's discretion, with electricity demand or contracted capacity exceeding 25 MW and not operating before 2026-07-01. Certification follows applicable notice and hearing and requires specified findings on rates, reliability, utility compliance, clean-energy policy and public interest; review includes grid capacity, environmental and public-health impacts and cross-subsidy. An adequate showing of specified contracts or other measures designed to offset system peak demand creates presumptions on certain findings, not an exemption from the certificate requirement.

fields.key_provisions: Enrolled HB1601 would require a locality, before approval of specified zoning applications for a new high energy use facility, to require the applicant to assess its sound profile on residential units and schools within 500 feet of the property boundary, to the extent practicable and within the statutory timeline. A facility qualifies when the applicant reasonably anticipates at application that it will require 100 MW or more of retail utility power. The locality may require specified resource assessments on the site or immediately contiguous land, and must require qualified utility substation and transmission information. The existing-approval expansion or modification exception states that the expansion 'does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more'; its numeric boundary is unresolved. Existing local zoning authority is preserved. The enrolled print has blank chapter and approval fields; later post-veto proceedings remain unverified.

fields.key_provisions: Introduced HB503 would bar inclusion in SCC-approved rates or charges under § 56-585.1 or § 56-585.8 of Phase I or Phase II utility costs, including increased fuel, generation and transmission costs, that are substantially related to electric service to data center customers and would not have been incurred but for their demand, unless the rates or charges are designed to recover, or substantially recover, those costs solely from data center customers. For this provision, a data center customer is a data center under § 58.1-3506(A)(43) with peak demand of 100 MW or greater.

fields.key_provisions: Observed code site-assessment framework requires an applicant's sound assessment before specified local approvals for a new facility reasonably anticipated to require at least 100 MW of retail utility power. Sound impacts concern homes and schools within 500 feet of the facility property boundary; other resource assessments are optional, and utility substation/voltage information is also required subject to stated qualifications. The framework preserves the existing-approval/expansion exception; its phrase “does not exceed an additional 100 megawatts or more” is not converted into a definitive boundary here. The observed code publishes the framework as 15.2-2209.5 and cites chapters 567 and 568. SB94's own chapter 568 print was not recovered in the inspected cohort; its printed section number remains unverified. Later force is not independently confirmed.

evidence.supports: Observed code supports framework; companion HB153 chapter567 cannot establish target SB94 chapter568 printed section number.
